entries.name: Excel MCP server (live COM, .NET) — Click-to-Run / Microsoft 365
entries.summary: Automate Microsoft Excel through its native COM API — Power Query, DAX measures, PivotTables, charts, formatting, and VBA macros (25 tools / ~230 operations) with real recalc against the live Excel process. Community server sbroenne/mcp-server-excel (C#/.NET 10), pinned to release v1.8.70. Distributed as a self-contained mcp-excel.exe — download from the release ZIP and add to PATH (see vendored_source.install_cmd); the launch command is the bare `mcp-excel` binary, not uvx. disabled-until-probe: enables only when Excel AND the mcp-excel server binary are present. PROBE SCOPE: this row targets a Click-to-Run / Microsoft 365 Excel install (the C:\Program Files*\Microsoft Office\root\Office1?\EXCEL.EXE layout, where the `root\` segment is the Click-to-Run signature). MSI / volume-license installs lay EXCEL.EXE down WITHOUT the `root\` segment (…\Microsoft Office\Office16\EXCEL.EXE), so the host-detect probe does NOT cover them in this batch — filepath.Glob has no `**` and the install_probe uses AND-semantics across entries, so it cannot OR the optional `root\` across two patterns. A file_globs[] OR-group probe model covering Click-to-Run + MSI + macOS is the tracked D-3 follow-up. The VBA-exec / RunMacro operations execute arbitrary code in the live workbook — gate the 6 VBA-exec ops behind operator consent (D-4). Windows + Click-to-Run Excel desktop only.

vendored_source.install_cmd: download mcp-excel.exe from the v1.8.70 release ZIP (https://github.com/sbroenne/mcp-server-excel/releases/tag/v1.8.70), extract to a tools dir, and add that dir to PATH

entries.name: Ableton Live MCP server
entries.summary: Control Ableton Live over a TCP socket — create/edit tracks, clips, devices, and transport via the Live Object Model. Community server ahujasid/ableton-mcp (Python, MIT), pinned to an immutable upstream commit and run via uvx from that git source. disabled-until-probe: enables only when a SUPPORTED Ableton Live is installed. REQUIRES Ableton Live 10 or newer — ahujasid/ableton-mcp's README advertises 'Ableton Live 10 or newer' and does NOT support Live 9 or earlier; the install probe therefore narrows to Live 10-19 via the glob C:\ProgramData\Ableton\Live 1[0-9]*\Program\Ableton Live 1[0-9]*.exe (the 1[0-9] char-class matches Live 10-19 across all editions Suite/Standard/Intro/Lite and EXCLUDES Live 9 and earlier, whose version segment does not begin with '1' followed by a digit), so a host with only an unsupported pre-10 install does not falsely pass admission for a server it cannot drive. Live 20+ (when released) will need a glob update — file_globs[] entries are AND-semantics and cannot OR a second version range, so a second range is a follow-up. macOS (/Applications/Ableton Live *.app) is NOT covered in this batch — the install_probe uses AND-semantics across entries and cannot OR a second install root, so a macOS row (or file_globs[] OR-group support) is a follow-up. PRIVACY: the pinned ableton-mcp ships telemetry ON by default (anonymous usage data sent to the upstream); this curated row sets ABLETON_MCP_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true in env to DISABLE the telemetry sender (no usage data leaves your machine), but note a one-time startup telemetry-status line may still log to the daemon stderr (cosmetic, upstream — the data send itself is off). SETUP (operator-side, REQUIRED): install the bundled Ableton Remote Script into Live's MIDI Remote Scripts directory and load it in Live — the MCP server connects to that script over a local TCP socket on port 9877; the host-exe probe detects Live, NOT the Remote Script, so verify the script is loaded before use. SECURITY (upstream limitation): the Remote Script you install into Live binds HOST=0.0.0.0:9877, so Ableton control is reachable from your LAN, not just localhost. Restrict port 9877 to loopback via your firewall, or only run on a trusted network. This is upstream ahujasid/ableton-mcp's bind (the hub cannot patch the operator-installed Remote Script); tracked for an upstream loopback fix.

entries.name: Codex MCP server (OpenAI Codex CLI)
entries.summary: Expose the OpenAI Codex CLI as an MCP server (`codex mcp-server`, stdio) so agents can call codex as a tool (codex() / codex-reply()). Official Codex CLI subcommand — NOT a community fork, so no vendored_source/pin. disabled-until-probe: enables only when the `codex` binary is on PATH. Keep the direct invoke-codex-prompt.sh path for orchestration/commission (file-based, governance); this row is for agents calling codex-as-tool.

entries.name: MATLAB MCP server (official, MathWorks)
entries.summary: Run MATLAB from an AI client — execute code, scripts, and functions against a live MATLAB process via the official MathWorks Go MCP server (matlab-mcp-server, stdio). OFFICIAL MathWorks server (matlab/matlab-mcp-server, pinned to release v0.11.0) — NOT a community fork, so no vendored_source (like the codex row). Distributed as a self-contained matlab-mcp-server binary: download matlab-mcp-server-windows-x64.exe from the v0.11.0 release and add it to PATH (rename to matlab-mcp-server), OR `go install github.com/matlab/matlab-mcp-server/cmd/matlab-mcp-server@latest`. REQUIRES a host MATLAB R2021a-or-later install ON THE SYSTEM PATH — by default the server finds the first MATLAB on PATH (it can also be pointed at one via --matlab-root / the MW_MCP_SERVER_MATLAB_ROOT env var, but this row sets no args/env so PATH is the only discovery), then drives the live MATLAB engine, so executing MATLAB code runs arbitrary host computation; the operator gates that the same way they gate any code-exec tool. disabled-until-probe: enables only when BOTH the matlab-mcp-server binary AND the `matlab` launcher are on PATH — the probe (binaries: matlab-mcp-server + matlab) AGREES with the server's own PATH discovery, so a MATLAB installed but NOT on PATH does not falsely enable the row. If you keep MATLAB off PATH, pass --matlab-root=<MATLAB root> (or set MW_MCP_SERVER_MATLAB_ROOT) in the manifest after install. License: MathWorks custom (BSD-style, with a clause restricting use to MathWorks products).

entries.name: Ansys MAPDL MCP server (PyMAPDL)
entries.summary: Drive Ansys MAPDL (Mechanical APDL) from an AI client through PyMAPDL — launch/connect to a MAPDL session and run finite-element analysis. Official Ansys server ansys/pymapdl-mcp (Python, FastMCP, stdio), pinned to release v0.2.1; published on PyPI as ansys-mapdl-mcp, run via uvx with the version pinned in args (like serena's pinned uvx source), so no vendored_source (official Ansys-org package, Apache-2.0). disabled-until-probe: enables only when an Ansys MAPDL install is detected via the version-agnostic glob C:\Program Files\ANSYS Inc\v*\ansys\bin\winx64\ansys*.exe — the Ansys solver executable is itself version-stamped (ansys241.exe for 2024 R1, etc.) under a v<ver> root (v231/v241/...). REQUIRES Python + uv on PATH and a host Ansys MAPDL install — the MAPDL-launching tools (launch_mapdl_session / connect_to_mapdl / disconnect_from_mapdl) start or attach to the solver and run arbitrary APDL, so the operator gates those raw solver/run tools behind consent the same way as any code-exec surface (D-4). Windows + Ansys MAPDL desktop only in this probe.

entries.name: KiCad MCP server
entries.summary: Drive KiCad EDA from an AI client — PCB design, DRC, simulation, BOM, DFM, manufacturing — through kicad-cli and the KiCad IPC / SWIG scripting API. Community server oaslananka/kicad-mcp (Python), published to PyPI as kicad-mcp-pro, pinned to v3.14.1 and run via uvx with the version pinned in --from (vendored_source block, community fork, MIT). PRIVACY: telemetry is OFF by default (OTLP export is opt-in to an operator-supplied collector), no telemetry-disable env needed. SAFETY: remote tools are read-only by default; destructive operations (board/schematic writes, manufacturing output) require explicit operator consent. disabled-until-probe: enables when uvx is on PATH AND a host KiCad 10.x install is detected via the glob C:\Program Files\KiCad\1[0-9]*\bin\kicad-cli.exe — per the server's compatibility.yaml, kicad-mcp-pro v3.14.1 targets KiCad 10.0.x as the PRIMARY supported line (KiCad 9.x was dropped/EOL after 10.0.0; 8.x is deprecated file-level-only; 7.x unsupported), so the gate matches the 10.x-and-newer roots only. REQUIRES Python 3.13+ and uv on PATH, plus a host KiCad 10.x install. Windows + KiCad desktop only in this probe.

entries.name: Suno AI Music (AceDataCloud)
entries.summary: Local AI music generation via Suno through the AceDataCloud API — runs the official mcp-suno PyPI package locally over stdio with uvx (no hosted endpoint). 27 tools spanning music generation, lyrics, media conversion, persona management, and task queries. REQUIRES an AceDataCloud API token: sign up at https://platform.acedata.cloud and mint a token on the API documentation page, then store it in the mcphub vault as the `acedata_api_token` secret (env ACEDATACLOUD_API_TOKEN = secret:acedata_api_token). The token is a REQUIRED install gate (required_secrets) — the local mcp-suno server hard-exits (exit 1) on startup when the token is unset, so a one-click install with no token is BLOCKED at install rather than crash-looping a daemon that returns 401s.

entries.name: Onshape MCP server
entries.summary: AI-assisted access to your Onshape cloud CAD documents — create sketches, extrude/revolve/sweep/fillet parts, build construction planes, take Part Studio screenshots, export STL/STEP, and write FeatureScript over the full Onshape REST API. Community server altendky/onshape-mcp, dual-licensed Apache-2.0 OR MIT (this row uses Apache-2.0). npx-packaged: the published onshape-mcp@0.4.0 npm package is a thin Node launcher around a per-platform Rust binary, run via `npx --yes onshape-mcp@0.4.0` (version pinned). PROVENANCE: onshape-mcp@0.4.0 is SLSA-provenance-attested and OIDC-published by the maintainer (altendky); the vendored_source pin is the v0.4.0 tag SHA. CLOUD — NO HOST APP: Onshape runs in the browser/cloud, so there is no local CAD install to detect; the install_probe gates only on the npx launcher being present, NOT a host binary. AUTH (two paths): the server's `auto` mode prefers OAuth (a browser login flow it walks you through on first use — no static credentials stored) OR Basic auth via Onshape API keys. To use API keys, store them in the mcphub vault and they wire to env ONSHAPE_MCP_AUTH__ACCESS_KEY = secret:onshape_access_key + ONSHAPE_MCP_AUTH__SECRET_KEY = secret:onshape_secret_key. These are OPTIONAL (not a required_secrets install gate) because OAuth is a valid alternative and the server does not hard-exit without API keys — it enters an OAuth-pending state and waits. D-4 CAVEAT: this is a CLOUD API-key (or OAuth) integration that can WRITE to your Onshape CAD documents (create/modify parts, export); supply credentials only through the hub vault, never as plaintext. PLATFORM: the published npm ships win32-x64 + linux/darwin (x64 + arm64) binaries but NOT win32-arm64 — on a Windows ARM64 host the launcher reports unsupported-platform at startup (a loud, clear error, not a silent failure). The binaries:[node,npx] probe gates on the Node launcher but cannot arch-gate (catalog-schema limitation shared by all launcher-based rows, e.g. KiCad's uvx probe); an arch-aware probe is a tracked follow-up. STATUS: early development — offered to try; some operations work more reliably than others at this stage.

entries.name: REAPER MCP server
entries.summary: Control the REAPER DAW from an AI client — 58 tools spanning project/transport, tracks, MIDI, items, FX, mixing, mastering, rendering, and audio analysis — driven through python-reapy against the REAPER Lua/Python Object Model. Community server bonfire-systems/reaper-mcp (Python), published to PyPI as reaper-mcp-server and pinned to v0.1.1, run via uvx with the version pinned in --from (vendored_source block, community fork, MIT). SECURITY (LAN exposure — SAME risk class as the Ableton row): the MCP server itself is stdio (`mcp.run(transport="stdio")` — no network listener), BUT the python-reapy distant API it requires runs a server INSIDE REAPER that binds 0.0.0.0 (upstream python-reapy Server.__init__ → `self.bind(("0.0.0.0", port))` in reapy/tools/network/server.py — verified), so once the distant API is enabled, REAPER control is reachable from your LAN, not just localhost. Restrict the reapy port to loopback via your firewall, or only run on a trusted network. This is upstream python-reapy's bind (the hub cannot patch the operator-enabled bridge). DESTRUCTIVE WRITE SURFACE: the 58 tools can MODIFY project state and files — save projects, delete tracks/items, import audio, render stems, change FX/mix params — so a one-click install grants an agent write access to your active music projects; work on COPIES/BACKUPS and treat destructive actions with caution. REQUIRED one-time operator setup (uvx install does NOT ship the repo's enable_reapy.py, and uvx does not install python-reapy into REAPER's Python, so use reapy's own canonical setup): SEPARATELY `pip install python-reapy`, then with REAPER OPEN run `python -c "import reapy; reapy.configure_reaper()"` (installs the reapy bridge into REAPER and enables the distant API — per the python-reapy README/install guide), then restart REAPER. The host-exe probe detects a REAPER install, NOT whether the distant API is configured, so complete this before first use. MATURITY: Alpha (pyproject Development Status :: 3 - Alpha; thin tests upstream) — offered to try, not all 58 tools are equally battle-tested. disabled-until-probe: enables when uvx is on PATH AND a host REAPER install is detected via the Windows glob C:\Program Files*\REAPER*\reaper.exe (the leading Files* covers BOTH the 64-bit C:\Program Files and the 32-bit C:\Program Files (x86) install roots; the default x64 install lands at C:\Program Files\REAPER (x64)\reaper.exe; the trailing-* on REAPER matches the version-suffixed variants). REQUIRES Python 3.10+ and uv on PATH plus a host REAPER install. macOS (/Applications/REAPER*.app) and Linux REAPER paths are NOT covered in this batch — file_globs[] entries are AND-semantics and cannot OR a second install root (same limit as the Ableton row), so a macOS/Linux probe is a follow-up.
